products.quality: Auto-selects the correct serial port; Devices window creates/edits multiple machine profiles via a guided wizard; per-device baud. Mature and well-documented, though USB/driver setup still trips some users (dedicated troubleshooting guide).

evidence.cite: https://docs.lightburnsoftware.com/latest/Reference/LaserWindow/ (auto serial-port select; Devices button; device dropdown)

products.quality: Directly connects to GRBL/Smoothieware over serial and Duet controllers over HTTP; Adding-Your-Machine wizard plus Devices window for profiles. Auto-port-detect not explicitly documented; shares LightBurn's device architecture.

Constantly scans available COM ports; user picks port and baud per GRBL config. Simple manual connect with soft-reset/home/unlock; no auto-connect or saved multi-machine profiles. Windows-only, GRBL 0.9/1.1 only.
Seamless auto-connect: 'XCS connects to your device automatically' over USB, Wi-Fi, or IP. Zero baud fuss for the user, but confined to xTool's own machines — no third-party controllers.

Guided Machine Setup wizard plus OEM partner machine profiles; connects through the locally installed Easel Driver. Cloud dependency: internet required to load/save projects and finish machine-profile setup.
Detects firmware flavour on connection and auto-selects grbl vs grblHAL; baud configurable in Config; machine-profile picker with Generic-CNC fallback. Widely praised as the best-UX free sender.

Move window offers $J continuous jogging, keyboard arrow jog, speed/step-size presets, Go to Origin, Home, and Show Last Position. Complete and daily-driven; movement shortcut keys documented and community-verified.

evidence.cite: https://docs.lightburnsoftware.com/latest/Reference/MoveWindow/ (continuous jog, speed/step presets, Go to Origin, Home)

products.quality: Control Mode Move window: Jog tab with variable speeds/step lengths, keyboard numpad and manual coordinate entry; Go To tab moves to coordinates or saved positions; machine/workpiece coordinate toggle.

evidence.cite: https://docs.millmagesoftware.com/latest/Reference/UI/ControlMode/ (Jog tab keyboard numpad; Go To saved positions)

products.quality: Directional jog buttons with a vertical speed slider and step-size slider; manual positioning plus home/unlock. Functional but basic — no continuous $J hold-jog or go-to-saved-position; keyboard jog limited.

Positioning is canvas/camera-driven with a low-power laser-spot and Aimed-measure targeting rather than a rich jog panel; basic directional moves exist. No speed presets or park-to-position workflow documented.

evidence.cite: No continuous-jog / speed-preset / park panel found across support.xtool.com 2026-07-13

products.quality: Jog panel moves X/Y/Z with selectable step intervals; a toggle enables keyboard-controlled movement. Adequate for setup; lacks continuous hold-jog, named speed presets, and go-to-saved-position controls.

Best-in-class: continuous jogging, 70+ keyboard shortcuts including shift+arrow axis jog, rapid/normal/precise speed presets, and go-to via six workspaces. Consistently cited as the standout free-sender jog experience.

Reference implementation: bounding-box Frame, Rubber-Band Frame (minimal irregular perimeter), Frame Continuously, and 'Laser on When Framing' low-power diode trace. Beginner framing guide plus one-key shortcuts; the roster standard.

evidence.cite: https://docs.lightburnsoftware.com/latest/Reference/LaserWindow/ (Frame, Rubber Band Frame, Frame Continuously, Laser on When Framing)

products.quality: Job Control window frames the job, applies tool-offset compensation by cut type, and can frame selected shapes. CNC-appropriate (no low-power trace — moves the tool around the bounds).

No native framing button; users build custom-button macros to trace a rectangular frame and turn the laser on at low power. Works but manual, rectangular-only, no rubber-band; longstanding built-in-framing request open.

Rect mode traces the rectangular boundary and Outline mode follows the object contour with the low-power laser point; strong consumer framing with camera-assisted preview. Positioning tolerance ~1-2 mm.

evidence.cite: https://support.xtool.com/article/1851 + https://support.xtool.com/article/2067 (Rect and Outline framing modes)

products.quality: No physical framing/outline feature found; Easel relies on on-screen toolpath simulation plus work-zero setting rather than tracing job bounds on the machine before carving.

evidence.cite: No framing/outline feature found across support.easel.com + forum.easel.com 2026-07-13

products.quality: Dedicated Outline button physically moves the machine around the job's rough perimeter to confirm dimensions and placement. Well-regarded; CNC (no low-power trace — spindle-off perimeter move).

Dedicated Fire button (enabled in Device Settings) fires the diode at a user-set low power for focus/alignment, with a power field; hold-Shift fires the beam while framing. The de-facto diode-alignment control.
CNC-router software with no laser; a diode-alignment fire/test-pulse is not applicable and is not present.
No dedicated fire button, but a custom-button macro turning the laser on at low power (M3 S-low) for focusing is a documented, common practice. Manual macro-based rather than one-click.

evidence.cite: https://forum.lightburnsoftware.com/t/how-do-i-turn-on-my-diode-at-low-power-to-focus-it-or-frame-a-job/10520 (cross-tool practice; LaserGRBL macro equivalents on FB group)

products.quality: Laser-spot mode emits a low-power beam to locate the start position, plus a red-cross positioning indicator; guided consumer alignment rather than a raw pulse-fire control. ~1-2 mm offset, user-calibratable.

evidence.cite: https://support.xtool.com/article/501 (Set the Laser Positioning Mode: laser spot, red cross)

products.quality: CNC-router (spindle) software with no laser diode; a fire/test-pulse alignment control is not applicable and is not present.

evidence.cite: https://easel.inventables.com/ (X-Carve/CNC router product; no laser fire control)

products.quality: grbl/grblHAL CNC sender with no laser-diode fire/test-pulse feature; diode-alignment pulsing is out of its spindle-CNC scope.

evidence.cite: https://github.com/Sienci-Labs/gsender (grbl/grblHAL CNC control; no laser fire control)

products.quality: Console Window sends raw G-code and shows controller responses; the 2.0 Macros Window creates unlimited named macro buttons with right-click editing. Comprehensive manual-command surface.
Console Window displays controller traffic and accepts direct manual commands; Macros Window stores and quickly sends frequently used commands. Mirrors LightBurn's console/macro model.

Command box enqueues any typed G-code line with an execution/error log; custom buttons act as macros supporting variables and math expressions in square brackets. Capable manual surface for its class.
Closed consumer app exposes no raw-G-code console or user-defined macro buttons; interaction is button/canvas-driven. Inferred absent from documentation across the support center.

evidence.cite: No console/terminal or user-macro feature found across support.xtool.com 2026-07-13

products.quality: Machine Inspector (Ctrl+Shift+D) has a Console field to send GRBL $-commands one at a time ($$, $21=0). Manual-command entry exists, but there are no user-defined macro buttons.

Console tab shows a true view of computer<->CNC communication and sends commands; Macros are rearrangeable with enhanced variables and individually assignable keyboard shortcuts. Strong, polished implementation.

Machine Settings window shows a formatted, labeled $$ firmware-settings table (edit/copy/reset); coordinate readout and Disconnected/Ready/Busy/Framing status. Alarm messages surface in the Console but aren't richly decoded into plain-English fixes.
Tool position shown in both machine and workpiece coordinates with a color-coded wireframe; Machine Settings window views/edits GRBL firmware settings. Alarm-code decoding not documented.

Displays machine state (Idle/Run/Alarm) with $X-unlock / $H guidance for alarm exit, runtime position in the preview, and a GRBL Configuration grid editing $$ settings. Solid basics, minimal alarm explanation.
Closed ecosystem: shows firmware version and processing status only — no user $$ firmware-settings editor, no GRBL-style DRO, and no alarm-code decoding surface. Status is camera/preview-oriented.

evidence.cite: No $$ firmware editor / machine-coordinate DRO / alarm decoding found on support.xtool.com 2026-07-13

products.quality: Machine Inspector reads/edits GRBL firmware settings and checks homing-switch status; jog panel shows position. Alarm handling is present but not a rich decode; a documented $-settings reference backs it.

Likely sector-leading: 3-axis DRO with manual value entry, an alarm/error Helper (hover the '?' for plain-English detail), and an EEPROM editor replacing the legacy firmware tool for GRBL settings/flashing.

Buffered transfer mode (default, faster) with a Synchronous fallback for incompatible controllers, plus DTR handling. Robust in practice, but the classic GRBL-over-USB limitation stands: a disconnect stops the job unrecoverably (community reports).

Streams jobs to GRBL/Smoothieware/Duet via Control Mode. Buffering strategy and long-job stability are not documented and the product is young (0.8.x); robustness stands at existence-level, not community-proven.

evidence.cite: No buffering/throughput/long-job-stability documentation found for MillMage 0.8.x 2026-07-13

products.quality: Streams G-code to grbl with line-count and time projection. Generally works, but community reports stalls/halts mid-job on some setups (buffer/comms), with no disconnect recovery. Dormant project (v7.14.1, ~16 months no release).

Sends the job to xTool machines over USB or Wi-Fi; work can run on-device (physical start button), so streaming interruptions matter less than for a live-USB sender. Closed pipeline; buffering internals undocumented.

evidence.cite: No buffering/throughput internals documented for XCS/Studio 2026-07-13

products.quality: Streams through the local Easel Driver; once a project is loaded, carving continues offline. Browser-tab/cloud model means a closed tab or lost driver connection risks the run; no line-level disconnect recovery documented.

The roster's job-recovery/robustness reference: development prioritizes interface reliability over features, start-from-line resumes an aborted/failed job, and it is widely cited as the most stable free sender for long jobs. [HW-limited: design + community signal.]
Devices window holds any number of machine profiles selected from the Laser-window dropdown; switch machines instantly (one active connection at a time). Standard, reliable multi-profile management.

Devices window lists all added machines, supports Make Default, duplicate, and import/export of .mmzip/.mmdev profiles for backup or transfer. Full multi-profile management (one active machine at a time).
No saved machine-profile system; you select a COM port and settings are global to the single connected machine. Managing multiple machines means manual reconfiguration each time.

evidence.cite: No multi-machine profile management documented for LaserGRBL 2026-07-13

products.quality: Connection interface supports multiple xTool devices with per-machine profiles; switch the active device in the app. Confined to xTool's own hardware lineup.

evidence.cite: https://support.xtool.com/article/1580 (support for multiple devices via the connection interface)

products.quality: Account-based machine profiles via the Machine Setup wizard and OEM partner profiles; select the machine per project. Cloud-stored profiles, one active machine per carving session.
Machine-profile picker with many presets plus Generic-CNC fallback, and up to six saved workspaces/zero positions switchable on the fly. Profile-based, one active machine per connection.
